newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's General Malan acquitted in murder trial.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's General Malan acquitted in murder trial.

text.p: Former South African defence minister Magnus Malan, the most senior figure to be tried for atrocities against blacks, was acquitted of all charges against him, including murder, attempted murder and conspiracy to murder, a judge ruled on Friday.
Judge Jan Hugo also acquitted all the remaining co-defendants on all charges.

The judge said there was no proof that military had planned a massacre in which 13 blacks were killed in a hamlet near the Indian Ocean port of Durban, or that they had set up death squads to carry out political attacks.

The judge rejected the evidence of state witnesses in the prosecution's case in South Africa's biggest apartheid-era "dirty war" trial against Malan, the most senior apartheid-era leader to be tried for atrocities.
South Africa does not operate a jury system. Rulings are made by a judge in consultation with two assessors.
